baseline_models.focus_anchor: The first-person pronoun is joined to رَبُّكُمُ and capped by ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ inside an introduced utterance.
baseline_models.mechanism: Vocalized speech annexes the hearers to the speaker through the second-person possessive, while lordship as ownership and sovereignty is intensified into unsurpassed rank and domination.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies speech brought out in articulation, making the claim an addressed verbal act rather than a private thought.
The branch supplies ownership, mastery, and obeyed sovereignty as the status being annexed.
The branch supplies prevailing and taking mastery over another, turning height into asserted supremacy.

changed_reading.before: He states that he is the hearers' highest lord.
changed_reading.after: He uses direct speech to appropriate the hearers as subjects and to make that claimed sovereignty unsurpassable.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: رَبُّكُمُ can name the one who tends and completes what belongs to him, not only a titled ruler.
baseline_models.mechanism: The possessive claim reaches into formation and maintenance: the speaker presents himself as the one who brings the audience along stage by stage, then converts that caretaking relation into supreme control through ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ.

activation_trace.role: The branch supplies tending, repairing, educating, and bringing a thing to completion as the claimed relation to the audience.
The branch supplies self-exaltation and domineering elevation, corrupting formative care into a boast of superiority.

changed_reading.before: رَبُّكُمُ is a bare sovereign title.
changed_reading.after: The speaker claims authorship of the hearers' formation and welfare, then weaponizes that intimate dependence as supreme domination.

context_deltas.mechanism: The surah supplies a prior model of governance as arranging an affair with regard to its outcome and exercising authority over command. Against that functional standard, the focus claim becomes a title asserted without the enacted administration that would substantiate lordship.

activation_trace.role: Lordship supplies the claimed domain of sovereignty that the contextual functions test.
Deliberate management with attention to consequences supplies enacted governance as a functional criterion for the claim.
Authority and the holder of command supply the jurisdiction that accompanies real administration.

structural_cues: 79:5 couples management and command before the eschatological and Pharaoh sequences.
The focus root ر ب ب recurs at 79:16, 79:19, 79:40, and 79:44 outside Pharaoh's sentence.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies management toward outcomes and authority over command; I infer that a lordship claim is measured by those enacted functions, so Pharaoh's self-naming is counterfeit. A live alternative is that 79:5 concerns delegated agents and only indirectly calibrates رَبّ.

changed_reading.before: The sentence is a maximal claim to sovereign status.
changed_reading.after: The sentence is an unsupported substitution of sovereign title for the outcome-directed governance already displayed elsewhere in the surah.

context_deltas.mechanism: The same figure is introduced through boundary-transgression and later placed in the general class of one who transgresses; the alternate branch image of water rising beyond bounds gives his ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ a material logic of overflow. His claimed height is therefore not stable elevation but excess past a rightful limit.

activation_trace.role: Blameworthy self-exaltation supplies the focus claim's upward vector.
Exceeding the boundary in disobedience defines the speaker before the claim and makes his elevation an overstep.
Water-like overflow supplies a concrete image for an elevation that escapes its proper bounds.

structural_cues: 79:17 labels Pharaoh's condition before the invitation and sign; 79:37 repeats the same root as an eschatological type after his story.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies moral boundary-crossing and a branch image of overflowing water; I infer an upward arrow from overflow to the superlative ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ. The alternative is to keep طغيان purely ethical, in which case it still marks the boast as illicit without adding spatial texture.

changed_reading.before: ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ denotes the top rank the speaker claims to occupy.
changed_reading.after: ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ voices transgression as over-height: a surge beyond legitimate limits masquerading as settled supremacy.

context_deltas.mechanism: Immediately before the denial and proclamation, Pharaoh is made to see a manifest, great sign. His later spoken superlative thus functions as a counter-display: verbal self-magnification attempts to overwrite evidence that was shown rather than merely reported.

activation_trace.role: Articulated speech supplies the medium by which the speaker answers visible evidence.
Elevation in honor and rank supplies the self-magnifying content of the counter-display.
Showing and making visible supplies presented evidence to which the later utterance reacts.
A manifest sign supplies an externally legible marker that resists the speaker's self-description.
Greatness and majesty supply the competing scale against which the claim to highest rank is heard.

structural_cues: 79:20 presents the great sign, 79:21 records denial and disobedience, and 79:24 culminates the reaction in speech.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies showing, a visible sign, greatness, denial, and then the focus utterance; I infer that the utterance is a rhetorical replacement for defeated evidence. Alternatively, ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ only grades the sign and need not be a direct lexical rival to ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ.

changed_reading.before: The boast independently announces the speaker's rank.
changed_reading.after: The boast is reactive counter-signage: speech tries to install the speaker's greatness after a greater claim has been made visible to him.

context_deltas.mechanism: The focus utterance is the endpoint of a political sequence: purposeful activity with a branch of administration over people, the driving together of a crowd, and a raised call. رَبُّكُمُ is therefore not merely descriptive theology; it is a mass-addressed bid to manufacture a governed constituency.

activation_trace.role: Externalized speech supplies the final verbal act in the mobilization sequence.
Mastery over the plural audience supplies the political relation the staging seeks to create.
The raised call supplies broadcast reach and turns the claim toward an assembled audience.
Administration and agency over a people supply a political possibility within the purposeful effort preceding the speech.
Driving and collecting a group toward one objective supplies the audience-making operation.

structural_cues: The tightly linked sequence ثُمَّ أَدْبَرَ يَسْعَىٰ / فَحَشَرَ فَنَادَىٰ / فَقَالَ makes the focus sentence the result of movement, gathering, and calling.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies purposeful motion, a branch of public administration, crowd collection, raised calling, and then speech; I infer a causal sequence of political staging that produces an addressable 'you.' The live alternative is a simpler narrative sequence with no technical apparatus of constituency-making.

changed_reading.before: The sentence is an individual's isolated boast.
changed_reading.after: The sentence is a staged proclamation whose plural possessive seeks to turn a collected crowd into the speaker's subjects.

context_deltas.mechanism: The immediate sequel captures the claimant, converts his fate into a punishment that restrains observers, and then makes the event transferable as an admonitory comparison. The proclamation's narrative function changes from triumphant climax to verbal evidence inside an exemplary case.

activation_trace.role: The articulated claim supplies the memorable evidence immediately subjected to reversal.
Being taken to account for wrongdoing supplies the direct reversal of the speaker's claimed untouchable rank.
Punishment that deters others turns the personal downfall into a socially transmitted warning.
Learning by carrying one condition over to another makes the focus claim reusable as an exemplary pattern.

structural_cues: The consecutive فَقَالَ / فَأَخَذَهُ links the boast directly to seizure, and 79:26 explicitly turns the episode outward toward one who fears.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies immediate accountability, deterrent punishment, and exemplary transfer; I infer that the quoted boast is preserved because it is evidence in the warning, not because it succeeds. Alternatively, the example may be Pharaoh's whole career rather than this sentence specifically.

changed_reading.before: The sentence is the peak of Pharaoh's self-presentation.
changed_reading.after: The sentence is the incriminating exhibit that the next two ayat seize and circulate as a deterrent example.

context_deltas.mechanism: The cosmic passage follows the failed claimant with height that is built, raised, and structurally supported. This material production of elevation exposes ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ as an adjective without works: actual highness belongs to an ordered construction beyond the speaker's scale, not to self-location by speech.

activation_trace.role: Literal rising and height supply the focus adjective's spatial face for comparison with the cosmic structure.
Joining parts into a construction supplies productive work behind the contextual height.
The act of making something high supplies achieved elevation rather than asserted elevation.
A roof that supports a built structure gives the raised height material coherence and stability.

structural_cues: 79:27 asks whether the human audience is harder to create than the sky; 79:28 answers with its raised and proportioned structure shortly after Pharaoh's fall.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies construction, raising, and a supporting roof; I infer that this enacted cosmic elevation is a scale-correction to Pharaoh's verbal superlative. The alternative is that the creation passage addresses resurrection capacity generally and only secondarily echoes the focus adjective.

changed_reading.before: The speaker places himself at the top of a political hierarchy.
changed_reading.after: His 'highest' is exposed as unbuilt verbal height when set beside an elevation actually constructed, raised, and ordered on a cosmic scale.

context_deltas.mechanism: The later diagnosis joins transgression to choosing ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, while the opposed path restrains the self from desire. Read back into the focus, the claimant's upward vocabulary masks a downward preference: the one saying 'highest' is governed by what is lower and by the self's inclination.

activation_trace.role: Self-exalting height supplies the upward surface that the later preference reverses.
Boundary-crossing disobedience carries Pharaoh's earlier characterization into the general afterlife diagnosis.
Deliberate preference supplies the choice that reveals what actually governs the self-exalting speaker.
The lower or nearer life supplies the downward pole concealed beneath the focus superlative.
The self's inclination supplies an internal ruler opposed to restraint and reveals dependency beneath claimed mastery.

structural_cues: 79:37 repeats Pharaoh's defining طغيان and 79:38 immediately explains the associated preference; 79:40 supplies the opposed self-restraint.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies transgression, preferential choice, the lower life, and inward inclination; I infer a vertical reversal in which the claimant to highest rank is actually subordinated to the lower. A live alternative is that الدنيا means nearer or present without carrying a morally spatial 'low' in this contrast.

changed_reading.before: The phrase claims maximal elevation over other lords.
changed_reading.after: The phrase is internally inverted: its speaker reaches verbally upward while his preference and desire place him under the lower life.

context_deltas.mechanism: Near the close, relation to the Lord is enacted as fearing a station before him, restraining the self, and recognizing the Hour's endpoint with him. These relations undo Pharaoh's possessive appropriation: a lord is not made by saying 'your Lord' to a crowd, but is the one before whom the self stands and with whom the final limit rests.

activation_trace.role: Claimed lordship and obeyed sovereignty supply the relation corrected by the closing ayat.
Fear in expectation of harm supplies an accountable subject's orientation toward lordship.
A station or standing place supplies the encounter in which sovereignty is experienced rather than proclaimed.
The limit at which a thing ends supplies final jurisdiction beyond any human claim.

structural_cues: 79:40 says مَقَامَ رَبِّهِۦ and 79:44 says إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ مُنتَهَىٰهَآ, changing both the pronoun and the direction of relation around the repeated focus root.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies fear, a station, an endpoint, and repeated رَبّ constructions; I infer that these enact the asymmetry Pharaoh tries to reverse by assigning himself to 'you.' Alternatively, the closing uses of رَبّ may correct the focus simply by reference, without the relational mechanics of standing and terminus.

changed_reading.before: رَبُّكُمُ lets the speaker define lordship by claiming possession of the audience.
changed_reading.after: The claim reverses the true relation: subjects stand before their Lord and final limits return to him; a crowd's possessive address cannot confer that position.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: It is surprising to compare Pharaoh's sentence with the eschatological rebuke because the two speech events have different agents and settings. It remains anchored in focus قَالَ and in the packet's voiced, single rebuke, which creates a sharp contrast between claimed and effective command. Downstream prose should present this as an acoustic-functional echo, not identify the two utterances.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قَالَ makes the boast a candidate act of commanding speech rather than only propositional content.

activation_trace.role: The form-distant branch of imposing judgment over another supplies the boast's attempted performative force.
A rebuking vocal cry supplies speech whose authority is demonstrated by its consequence.
Singularity and separateness sharpen the contrast between one effective cry and an elaborate claim to command.

changed_reading.before: Pharaoh's utterance sounds powerful because it asserts the highest authority.
changed_reading.after: It sounds like counterfeit effective speech when the surah has already depicted a single rebuke whose authority lies in what it actually brings about.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's non-dominant ق ل ل mapping for focus ق و ل and must not be presented as the verb's ordinary morphology. It remains packet-anchored through that explicit split target and converges visibly with focus ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ. Downstream prose should label it a form-distant lexical echo: the utterance figuratively crowns its speaker rather than lexically meaning 'summit.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: قَالَ and ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ occur in the same compact assertion, while the supplied split inventory maps the speech root to a branch of summit or head.

activation_trace.role: The non-dominant summit or head image makes the speech itself figuratively function as an attempted crowning point.
Literal height lets the form-distant summit image converge on the explicit superlative rather than float free of the ayah.

changed_reading.before: قَالَ merely introduces the content of a boast about rank.
changed_reading.after: As an exploratory echo, the act of saying becomes the summit on which the speaker tries to place and crown himself.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the packet's secondary ر ب و target beneath focus ر ب ب, so it cannot replace the ordinary sense of رَبّ. It remains anchored by the supplied split mapping and by the adjacent explicit root of height. Downstream prose should describe a possible doubling or escalation of upward imagery, not translate رَبُّكُمُ as 'your rising one.'
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The split target under رَبُّكُمُ contributes increase and rise immediately before the explicit superlative ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ.

activation_trace.role: The secondary target contributes increase and rising as an exploratory undertone within the lordship claim.
Explicit elevation receives and intensifies the secondary rising image into a doubled upward movement.

changed_reading.before: رَبُّكُمُ names a status and ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ separately grades it.
changed_reading.after: The phrase may enact escalating self-elevation twice, with a faint rise inside the split lordship inventory that is then overtly capped by 'highest.'

strongest_changes: The boast becomes the endpoint of crowd collection and raised public address, so رَبُّكُمُ actively manufactures a constituency.
Prior transgression and later preference for the lower life invert ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ: apparent height masks boundary-overflow and subjection to what is lower.
The shown great sign makes the sentence reactive counter-signage rather than an independent declaration.
Built and raised cosmic height, followed by the true station and terminus of lordship, tests the unsupported verbal superlative against enacted authority.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah context activated three distinct mechanisms that a local reading could collapse: political staging before the line, material and moral vertical reversals after it, and a closing relational correction in which lordship is encountered as station and endpoint. The packet's split mappings also preserved form-distant summit and double-rise echoes as contained outliers.
remaining_uncertainties: The political sense of سَعْي as administration over people is branch-supported but more distant than ordinary purposeful movement in 79:22.
The cosmic height passage may primarily argue for resurrection rather than directly answer Pharaoh's superlative.
The lower/nearer range of د ن و leaves some uncertainty about how strongly spatial 'lowness' should be heard against ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ.
The ق ل ل and ر ب و outliers depend on explicit packet split mappings and should remain echoes, not lexical translations.
